spans.s:
दैव a. (वी f.) [देवादागतः अण्]
Relating to gods, caused by or
coming from gods, divine, celestial;
संस्कृतं नाम दैवी वागन्वाख्याता महर्षिभिः

.
--वः (i. e. विवाहः) One of the eight
forms of marriage, that in which
the daughter is given away at a
sacrifice to the officiating priest;
यज्ञस्य ऋत्विजे दैवः

; (for
the eight forms of marriage see उद्वाह
or

).
--वं
1 Fate, destiny,
luck, fortune; दैवमविद्वांसः प्रमाणयंति

; विना पुरुषकारेण दैवमत्र न
सिध्यति ‘God helps those who help
[]
themselves’; दैवं निहत्य कुरु
पौरुषम त्मशक्त्या

. (दैवात् by
chance, luckily, accidentally).
--2
A god, deity.
--3 A religious rite or
offering, an oblation to gods.
--4 A
kind of Śrāddha ceremony.
--5 Parts
of the hands sacred to the gods,
i. e. the tips of the fingers; cf.

.
--वी A woman married
according to the form of marriage
called daiva q. v. above.
--Comp.
--अत्ययः evil resulting from
unusual natural phenomena.
--अधीन
--आयत्त a. dependent on fate;
दैवायत्तं कुले जन्म मदायत्तं तु पौरुषं

.
--अहोरात्रः a day of the gods.
i. e. the human year.
--उपहत a.
illfated, unfortunate;

.
--कर्नन् n. offering oblations to gods.
--कृत a. {1} fated. {2} natural.
--कोविद्, --चिंतकः, --ज्ञः an astrologer, a
fortune-teller;

.
--तंत्र a.
dependent on fate.
--दीपः the eye.
--दुर्विपाकः hardness of fortune,
adverseness or unpropitiousness of
fate, an evil turn of fate;

.
--योगः a lucky
coincidence, fortuitous combination,
fortune, chance; (दैवयोगेन, दैवयोगात्
fortunately, accidentally).
--लेखकः
a fortune-teller, an astrologer.
--वशः, --शं the power of destiny,
subjection to fate.
--वाणी {1} a voice from
heaven. {2} the Sanskrit language;
cf.

quoted above.
--हीन
a. ill-fated, unfortunate, unlucky.

दैवत a. (ती f.) [देवता-अण्]
1
Divine.
--2 (At the end of an adj.
comp.) Honouring or worshipping as
one's deity, as in सूर्यदैवता जनाः.
--तं
1 A
god, deity, divinity; मृदं गा दैवतं विप्र
घृतं मधु चतुष्पदं प्रदक्षिणानि कुर्वीत

.
--2
A number of gods, the whole class
of gods;

.
--3 An idol. (The
word is said to be m. also, but is
[]
rarely used in that gender.
Mammaṭa notices it as a fault called
अप्रयुक्तत्व; see अप्रयुक्त).
--4 N. of the
third Kāṇḍa of Yāska's Nirukta.

दैवतस् ind. By chance,
fortunately, luckily.

दैवत्य a. Addressed or sacred to
a deity;

दैविक a. (की f.) [देव-ठक्]
Relating to the gods, divine;

दैव्य a. (व्या or व्यी f.) Divine.
--व्यं
1 Fortune, fate.
--2 Divine
power.

दैवलः, --लकः The servant of
an evil spirit.

दैवलः, --लकः The servant of
an evil spirit.

दैवासुरं The natural enmity
subsisting between the gods and the
demons.
